points.why: It names the vacancies→overtime→burnout→departures reinforcing loop but never frames mandatory overtime as a quick fix that backfires (Fixes That Fail).
It places (a) as a parameter on the departure link, (b) as a rule on the overtime→burnout link, and (c) as the goal, explaining how answer-time-only evaluation makes overtime look necessary.
Its table rates power and reach separately and notes (c) needs outside approval while (a) is easy but weak, but it never suggests testing the options in a model.
It chooses clearly, labels (a) a stopgap that buys time for (b), frames (c) as what protects (b), and flags the answer-time dip and training gap as short-term costs.

pitfalls.why: It keeps the bonus as a targeted overtime premium and leads with the cap rather than dismissing either for being low-leverage.
